strengths: Clear problem motivation: articulates specific limitations of unconstrained LS fitting (geometric distortion, overparameterization, coupling) with compelling intuition
Principled mathematical framework: elegant formulation of compensation as Orthogonal Procrustes problem with closed-form solution
Simple and practical: no architectural changes required, modest O(d³_out) overhead, directly integrable with existing methods like WANDA-sp
Consistent empirical improvements: outperforms WANDA-sp across all pruning ratios (10-30%) on both perplexity and benchmark tasks
Comprehensive ablations: good analysis of where to apply rotation (Table 3), impact of variance term (Figure 2), and method components
Well-presented: clear figures, algorithm descriptions, and generally well-written exposition
weaknesses: Limited novelty: applies classical Orthogonal Procrustes problem and adds single variance term to existing WANDA-sp score, representing incremental rather than fundamental contribution
Narrow experimental scope: single model (LLaMA-7B only), no evaluation on 13B/70B where pruning is critical, no other architectures, severely limiting generalizability claims
Modest improvements over FLAP: only 4.4% at 10%, 6.2% at 20%, and 1.9% at 30% pruning; actually underperforms FLAP on mean benchmark accuracy at 30%
Insufficient calibration analysis: despite claiming to handle limited calibration, all experiments use 128 samples with no ablation on smaller sets, undermining core motivation
Limited baselines: compares only WANDA-sp and FLAP; missing comparisons with other recent structured pruning methods despite citing them
Weak justification for variance scoring: claim that variance predicts principal direction contributions lacks rigorous support; no analysis of scoring design choices
Incomplete mechanism analysis: limited empirical validation that outputs preserve geometric properties; unexplained why LS hurts dramatically with variance-aware but not WANDA-sp scoring
Greedy layerwise optimization: no discussion of alternatives or analysis of whether layer interactions matter; no joint global optimization
Stability concerns: method sometimes underperforms at 30% compression; limited discussion of failure modes or applicability limits
Reproducibility gaps: attention pruning procedure vaguely described, no code release mentioned, missing implementation details, no statistical significance testing

strengths: Well-motivated geometric approach with clear articulation of limitations of unconstrained least-squares fitting; principled Orthogonal Procrustes formulation with closed-form efficient solution
Practical simplicity and broad applicability: no architectural modifications, integrates seamlessly with existing pruning pipelines, modest computational overhead
Variance-aware pruning score is intuitive and empirically justified; shows clear benefits over WANDA-sp across all pruning ratios
Consistent improvements over WANDA-sp baseline across multiple metrics (perplexity and 7 language understanding benchmarks); results comparable or better than stronger FLAP baseline
Comprehensive experimental design with appropriate baselines, multiple pruning ratios, diverse evaluation metrics, and meaningful ablations (e.g., where to apply rotation)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations; logical progression from motivation to method to results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: applies classical Orthogonal Procrustes technique (Golub & Van Loan, 2013) in straightforward manner; variance-aware score is incremental extension of WANDA-sp
Marginal improvements over stronger baseline FLAP (0.59 PPL at 10%, 0.96 at 20%, 0.24 at 30%); inconsistent gains on individual benchmarks where RCPU sometimes underperforms WANDA-sp

Narrow experimental scope: single model (LLaMA-7B), single calibration dataset (WikiText-2 with 128 samples), no evaluation on larger models, limited baseline comparisons (missing SliceGPT, other recent 2024 methods)

Insufficient empirical validation of core claims: variance-aware scoring preserving principal directions lacks direct evidence; no visualization or analysis comparing selected columns to actual output principal directions; scaled variant (Rot.+Scale) provides negligible benefit, contradicting norm preservation motivation

Missing critical ablations: no sensitivity analysis on calibration set size, variance term weight, or robustness to calibration quality; no statistical significance testing, error bars, or confidence intervals

Shallow theoretical analysis: claim about reduced overfitting not rigorously justified; geometric preservation argument is loose since rotation preserves angles but pruning fundamentally changes effective geometry; greedy layer-wise optimization not justified vs. joint approaches

Computational efficiency concerns: O(d³_out) SVD overhead for structured pruning is substantial; Table 4 shows counter-intuitive scaling (longer time at higher pruning) due to GPU library inefficiency, raising scalability doubts
Limited analysis of failure modes and boundary conditions: no discussion of when dropped columns are essential, Procrustes solution quality, or error propagation across layers

strengths: Clear problem formulation with elegant mathematical solution using Orthogonal Procrustes problem, providing closed-form solution and principled geometric preservation without hyperparameter tuning
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Llama-7B, Llama-2-13B, Vicuna), pruning ratios (10%-30%), and calibration sizes, with both perplexity and downstream benchmark assessment
Consistent improvements over WANDA-sp and FLAP baselines across most settings, particularly pronounced at higher pruning ratios where rotation-constrained updates become more critical

Insightful analysis showing RCPU generalizes better to downstream tasks than LS+Ridge despite comparable perplexity, suggesting better preservation of pretrained knowledge with lower effective degrees of freedom
Practical applicability: no architectural modifications, modest computational overhead, and no hyperparameter selection required, making it deployable to production systems
Thoughtful ablation studies (layer-wise application, comparison with LS+Ridge variants, calibration size sensitivity) demonstrating understanding of method components
weaknesses: Limited novelty: applies classical Orthogonal Procrustes problem (well-known since Golub & Van Loan 2013) to post-pruning error compensation; variance-aware score is straightforward extension of WANDA-sp with limited innovation

Incremental empirical improvements: typically 4-6% PPL gain over FLAP baseline, with benchmark accuracy improvements often within noise margins; at 30% pruning, sometimes underperforms FLAP (Table 2: 55.50 vs 56.20)

Weak theoretical justification for variance-aware scoring: claim that high-variance columns affect principal directions lacks formal analysis; missing ablation study on individual scoring components; unclear why multiplicative form is optimal

Incomplete baseline comparisons: no evaluation against recent rotation-based methods (RotPruner, DenoiseRotator mentioned but not compared); SliceGPT comparison limited to Llama-2-13B; missing comparisons with other structured pruning approaches

Evaluation limitations: only WikiText-2 for calibration; no assessment of sensitivity to calibration data distribution; no statistical significance testing or error bars despite high variance in benchmark results; limited to transformer LLMs

Fairness concerns in hyperparameter selection: λ_best chosen on calibration set (Section 7.1) while RCPU requires no tuning, creating potential bias; Figures 5-6 show extreme λ sensitivity and instability, questioning LS+Ridge baseline robustness
Greedy layer-wise formulation not globally optimized; potential error compounding across layers not addressed; no comparison with joint optimization approaches

Missing technical justification: scaled variant provides minimal benefit over rotation-only, questioning its necessity; no analysis of when rotation constraint is sufficient; limited discussion of failure modes or architectural limitations
